hero.headline: Stay on top of your money — not buried in spreadsheets.
hero.subhead: Nixus automates the upkeep: upload a credit card statement, get categorized expenses, see your next move. Budget, TFSA, RRSP, net worth — on your machine, without Plaid.
trust.heading: Why you can trust Nixus with this
trust.local.title: Your records stay on your machine
trust.local.body: Budgets, transactions and balances live in a local database on your own computer. Nixus keeps no copy unless you turn on sync.
trust.noLogins.title: No bank passwords, ever
trust.noLogins.body: No Plaid, no screen-scraping, no credentials to hand over. You upload a statement instead.
trust.openSource.title: Open source
trust.openSource.body: The code that handles your finances is public, so you don't have to take any of this on faith.
trust.platforms.title: macOS and Windows
trust.platforms.body: A real desktop app, with automatic updates and database backup and restore built in.
pillars.heading: Rearview apps show your money. Nixus helps you stay on top of it.
pillars.subhead: Built for people who already track their own finances and won't hand bank credentials to a cloud service to do it.
pillars.automation.title: Automation without bank access
pillars.automation.description: Upload screenshots or PDFs — no Plaid, no passwords. AI extracts and categorizes in seconds.
pillars.automation.contrast: Most alternatives automate by asking for your bank login. Nixus automates the part that was actually tedious instead.
pillars.nextAction.title: Next action, not another chart
pillars.nextAction.description: Emergency fund runway, savings capacity, and one clear priority — not just dashboards.
pillars.nextAction.contrast: A chart tells you what happened. Nixus tells you what to do about it.
pillars.lifeUpkeep.title: One app for life upkeep
pillars.lifeUpkeep.description: Finance and car maintenance today — same shell, same local data. More modules over time.
pillars.lifeUpkeep.contrast: One install, one set of data, one place to look — not a separate app per responsibility.
howItWorks.heading: Three steps. About five minutes, every other week.
howItWorks.subhead: If you've never kept a budget, this is the entire routine. There's no setup marathon, and nothing to connect.
howItWorks.upload.title: Upload a statement
howItWorks.upload.body: Screenshot your credit card statement, or save it as a PDF, and drop it into Nixus.
howItWorks.categorize.title: Let it sort itself out
howItWorks.categorize.body: Nixus reads the statement, pulls out each transaction, and files it into a category — remembering your corrections for next time.
howItWorks.review.title: See where you stand
howItWorks.review.body: Scan what came in, fix anything that landed wrong, and your budget, cash flow, and net worth are already current.
howItWorks.review.detail: Then close it and get on with your day.
howItWorks.footnote: Prefer to type things in yourself? Manual entry covers everything, and the AI features are never required.

stages.heading: Four questions, in the order you'd actually ask them.
stages.subhead: Nixus is built in four stages. Each one answers a question, and each one is a real screen you can open today — not a roadmap promise.
stages.organize.heading: Everything in one place, without a bank password.
stages.organize.body: Upload a credit card statement as a screenshot or a PDF. Nixus reads it, pulls out every transaction, and files them into your categories. Accounts, investments, and the things you own go in once and stay current from there.
stages.organize.points.import: Statement in, categorized transactions out — no Plaid, no bank login, no waiting for a broken connection to come back.
stages.organize.points.accounts: Chequing, credit cards, savings, TFSA, RRSP, FHSA, non-registered and crypto — in CAD or USD, in one list.
stages.organize.points.assets: A house, a car, a business stake — the parts of your net worth a budgeting app usually ignores.
stages.organize.caption: Every account and asset in one view, with allocation by account type.
stages.organize.alt: Nixus accounts view listing balances across account types with an allocation breakdown
stages.understand.heading: The whole answer on one screen.
stages.understand.body: A budget you can read at a glance, cash flow that counts income against spending, and net worth tracked by category over time. These numbers are calculated, not estimated — no AI guessing at your balance.
stages.understand.points.budget: Monthly budgets with category groups, and a clear read on what's left before the month ends.
stages.understand.points.cashflow: Income recorded alongside expenses, so "can I afford this" has an actual answer.
stages.understand.points.netWorth: Net worth history split by cash, housing, crypto, TFSA and RRSP — not one blended line.
stages.understand.caption: The finance dashboard — budget, cash flow, and net worth together.
stages.understand.alt: Nixus finance dashboard showing budget remaining, cash flow, net worth, and spending by category
stages.guide.heading: A straight answer, in plain language.
stages.guide.body: Ask what you'd ask a friend who happened to know all your numbers. Nixus answers from your actual data, shows you how it got there, and waits for your confirmation before changing anything.
stages.guide.points.health: Emergency-fund runway, savings rate, and one priority action — rule-based, so the same numbers always give the same answer.
stages.guide.points.chat: "Can I afford a $40k car?" "Where did the extra $600 go last month?" Asked normally, answered from your data.
stages.guide.points.confirm: Nothing is edited behind your back. Every proposed change is shown to you first.
stages.guide.caption: Ask a question in plain language; the answer uses your real numbers.
stages.guide.alt: Nixus AI chat answering a budget question with category-level detail from the user's own data
stages.automate.heading: The upkeep that made you quit last time.
stages.automate.body: Recurring expenses apply themselves. Vehicle service comes due before you've forgotten about it. Updates install in the background. The work that killed your spreadsheet is the work Nixus is built to absorb.
stages.automate.points.recurring: Rent, insurance, subscriptions — set the template once and each month fills itself in.
stages.automate.points.maintenance: Every vehicle gets a maintenance schedule and a nudge before service is overdue, not after.
stages.automate.points.updates: Automatic updates and local backup and restore, so maintaining the tool isn't another chore.
stages.automate.caption: The garage — maintenance schedules and service due dates, per vehicle.
stages.automate.alt: Nixus garage view listing vehicle maintenance tasks with upcoming and overdue service
privacy.heading: Local-first, stated precisely.
privacy.subhead: The short version: your financial records are on your computer, not ours. The long version matters more — so here are the only two things that can ever leave it, and both are off until you turn them on.
privacy.stays.heading: Stays on your machine
privacy.stays.items.records: Budgets, transactions, accounts, income, assets, net worth history, vehicles and service records — in a local database on your device.
privacy.stays.items.credentials: Any AI provider credentials you enter, held in your operating system's keychain and never transmitted to Nixus.
privacy.stays.items.offline: Everything except the AI features works with no network connection at all.
privacy.exceptions.heading: The two exceptions
privacy.exceptions.intro: Neither one runs unless you choose it, and neither is on by default.
privacy.exceptions.items.ai.title: AI features
privacy.exceptions.items.ai.body: When you run an import or ask the AI a question, that one request's content is sent for processing — straight to your own provider using your credentials, or through Nixus to AWS Bedrock on a premium account. There's no background transmission, and the rest of the app works without it.
privacy.exceptions.items.sync.title: Multi-device sync
privacy.exceptions.items.sync.body: If you want the same records on a second computer, a copy is stored in Nixus-operated storage on AWS. It's encrypted in transit and at rest, but not end-to-end encrypted in this version — so a Nixus administrator could technically read it. Leave sync off and no copy leaves your machine.

isIsnt.is.items.canadian: Built around Canadian accounts — TFSA, RRSP, FHSA, with CAD and USD side by side.

faq.heading: Frequently asked
faq.bankConnection.question: Does this connect to my bank?
faq.bankConnection.answer: No, by design — unlike Monarch, YNAB, and most Mint replacements. You upload a credit card statement (screenshot or PDF) and the AI parses it. Nixus never asks for your bank login, never connects to Plaid, and doesn't pull data from your accounts. You stay in control.
faq.installSafety.question: Is this safe to install?
faq.installSafety.answer: Nixus is open source — you can inspect the code on GitHub. First-launch warnings (macOS Gatekeeper, Windows SmartScreen) are normal for apps not yet signed by Apple or trusted by Microsoft's reputation system. Install instructions appear after you click Download.
faq.isItFree.question: Is it free?
faq.isItFree.answer: Yes, free for now. The plan is a free tier plus paid modules later — the AI import feature is the most likely first paid module. When that ships, existing users will see clear pricing — no surprise charges.
faq.dataStorage.question: Where is my data stored?
faq.dataStorage.answer: Locally on your machine. Your budget, accounts, and net worth are stored in a local database on your device. There are two opt-in exceptions. The AI features: when you use them, that request's content is sent for processing — either straight to your own AI provider, or, on a premium Nixus Cloud account, through Nixus infrastructure to AWS Bedrock. And multi-device sync: if you turn it on, a copy of that profile's data is stored in Nixus's private storage on AWS so your other computers stay up to date. Both are off unless you choose them; the Privacy Policy describes each in detail.
faq.linuxSupport.question: Is Linux supported?
faq.linuxSupport.answer: Not in the alpha version. Linux support is on the roadmap but not committed. The macOS build may run via compatibility layers but isn't officially tested.
faq.mobileSupport.question: What about mobile?
faq.mobileSupport.answer: Nixus is a desktop app (macOS and Windows). There's no mobile app planned for the alpha version — the focus is on getting the desktop experience right first.
faq.whoBuilt.question: Who built this?
faq.whoBuilt.answer: One person — built because spreadsheets stopped scaling for my own finances. You can find me on GitHub, or reach out by email.
faq.howToUpdate.question: How do I update?
faq.howToUpdate.answer: Nothing to do — Nixus checks for updates automatically and installs them in the background. You'll always have the latest version next time you open the app.
faq.preAlpha.question: What does 'pre-alpha' mean?
faq.preAlpha.answer: Nixus is in pre-alpha: the core functionality is in place, and the product is actively evolving based on user feedback and where we take it from here. Things may change between releases. Your records stay on your machine unless you turn on multi-device sync, and auto-update keeps you on the latest version.

termsPage.heading: Terms of Service
termsPage.intro: Nixus is a local-first desktop app for personal finance and vehicle tracking. These terms govern your use of the app and of the optional Nixus Cloud services. Nixus is pre-alpha software provided as-is.
termsPage.acceptance.heading: Acceptance
termsPage.acceptance.body: By installing or using Nixus you agree to these terms and to the Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, do not use the app.
termsPage.aiFeatures.heading: AI features
termsPage.aiFeatures.body: Nixus includes optional AI features: credit card statement import, AI chat, project advice, and spending-trends insight. These features only run when you invoke them. Running them transmits that request's content — which may include financial transactions and an uploaded statement image or PDF — off your device for processing.
termsPage.aiFeatures.byo: By default you supply your own AI provider credentials (AWS Bedrock or OpenAI). Those requests go directly from your device to that provider under your own agreement with them, and Nixus infrastructure is not involved.
termsPage.aiFeatures.hosted: If your account has Nixus Cloud premium enabled, AI requests are instead transmitted through Nixus's own infrastructure to Amazon Bedrock, operated by Amazon Web Services. Nixus selects the model and applies a monthly limit on the number of requests. Processing uses a cross-region Bedrock inference profile scoped to the United States, so a request may be processed in any US AWS region, which may be outside your country of residence. See the Privacy Policy for exactly what is and is not retained.
termsPage.quota.heading: Request quota
termsPage.quota.body: Premium hosted AI is subject to a monthly request quota and to an overall service capacity limit, both set at Nixus's discretion and adjustable without notice. When your quota is exhausted, when the service is unavailable, or when hosted AI is disabled, Nixus falls back to any AI provider you have configured yourself where that provider supports the feature. Where no fallback is possible, the feature reports an error. No other part of the app is affected.
termsPage.accounts.heading: Accounts and premium access
termsPage.accounts.body: A Nixus Cloud account is required for hosted AI. Premium hosted-AI capability is granted manually and is entirely separate from any paid module license. Nixus may suspend or revoke hosted-AI access, including for abuse or excessive cost.
termsPage.noAdvice.heading: Not professional advice
termsPage.noAdvice.body: Nixus is a tracking tool. Nothing it produces — including AI-generated categorizations, advice, or insights — is tax, legal, accounting, or investment advice. AI output can be wrong. You are responsible for reviewing it before relying on it.
termsPage.yourData.heading: Your data and backups
termsPage.yourData.body: Your records are stored in a local database on your device. Nixus holds no copy of them unless you turn on multi-device sync, which stores a copy as described above and in the Privacy Policy. Nixus does not operate a backup service, and keeping your own backups is your responsibility.
termsPage.warranty.heading: Warranty and liability
termsPage.warranty.body: Nixus is pre-alpha and is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind. To the maximum extent permitted by law, Nixus and its author are not liable for any loss or damage arising from your use of the app, including data loss or decisions made from AI output.
termsPage.changes.heading: Changes
termsPage.changes.body: These terms may change as the product develops. Material changes affecting how your data is handled will be reflected here and in the Privacy Policy before the corresponding feature ships.

privacyPage.meta.title: Privacy Policy — Nixus
privacyPage.meta.description: What Nixus stores on your device, what leaves it when you use the AI features, what optional multi-device sync uploads and who can read it, and how Nixus Cloud premium hosted AI transmits content to AWS Bedrock.
privacyPage.heading: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.intro: Nixus is local-first: by default your financial records are stored on your own device and Nixus holds no copy of them. This policy explains the two things that change that, and both are off until you choose them: the optional AI features, and optional multi-device sync.
privacyPage.local.heading: What stays on your device
privacyPage.local.body: Budgets, transactions, accounts, income, assets, net worth history, vehicles, and maintenance records are stored only in a local database on your machine. There is no account required to use them and no bank connection. By default nothing is uploaded; the two exceptions are the AI features you invoke and multi-device sync, which you have to turn on yourself. AI provider credentials you enter are stored in your operating system's credential store, never transmitted to Nixus.
privacyPage.aiLeaves.heading: What leaves your device, and when
privacyPage.aiLeaves.body: Only when you invoke an AI feature. There is no background transmission. At that point the content of that single request leaves your device. Depending on your configuration that content goes to one of two places.
privacyPage.byo.heading: Your own AI provider
privacyPage.byo.body: By default, the request goes directly from your device to the provider you configured — AWS Bedrock or OpenAI — using your own credentials. Nixus infrastructure is not in that path and cannot see the request. That provider's own privacy terms apply.
privacyPage.hosted.heading: Nixus Cloud premium hosted AI
privacyPage.hosted.body: If premium hosted AI is enabled on your account, your financial prompts and any uploaded statement image or PDF are transmitted through Nixus's own infrastructure to Amazon Bedrock, operated by Amazon Web Services, for processing.
privacyPage.hosted.notRetained: Nixus does not store the prompt, the attached statement, the model's response, or the file name in its own databases or logs. Request content exists in Nixus's systems only in memory, for the duration of that one request.
privacyPage.hosted.retained: Nixus does record, and retain: your account identifier, the calendar month, which feature was used, timestamps, request latency, success or failure status, request counts, and token counts. These are used to enforce your quota and to operate the service.
privacyPage.limits.heading: Two limits on that guarantee
privacyPage.limits.aws: The non-retention guarantee above covers Nixus-controlled systems only. It does not bind Amazon Web Services. AWS may process and, under Bedrock's terms and its abuse-detection policies, retain request content. Nixus does not control or override that.
privacyPage.limits.processingRegion: Hosted AI uses a cross-region Amazon Bedrock inference profile scoped to the United States, so an individual request may be processed in any US AWS region and is not confined to a single one. That processing may be outside your country of residence, and AWS's terms for the handling region apply to it.
privacyPage.quota.heading: Request quota and fallback
privacyPage.quota.body: Hosted AI is subject to a monthly request quota. When it is exhausted, unavailable, or disabled, Nixus falls back to any AI provider you configured yourself where that provider supports the feature, and otherwise reports an error. Your records and the rest of the app are unaffected.
privacyPage.noSale.heading: No sale of personal information
privacyPage.noSale.body: Nixus does not sell your personal information and does not use your financial content to train models.
privacyPage.analytics.heading: Website analytics
privacyPage.analytics.body: This marketing website uses privacy-preserving aggregate analytics and does not have access to any data from the desktop app.
privacyPage.contact.heading: Contact
privacyPage.contact.body: Questions about this policy, or a request concerning your data:
termsPage.aiFeatures.precedence: On a premium account, hosted AI takes precedence: an eligible request is sent through Nixus to Amazon Bedrock even when you have configured your own AI provider for that feature. Nixus does not offer an in-app setting to choose between them. Your own provider is used only when hosted AI is unavailable, when your monthly quota is exhausted, or when your account is not premium.
privacyPage.hosted.precedence: Note which path a request takes. On a premium account, an eligible request goes through Nixus to Amazon Bedrock even if you have entered your own AWS or OpenAI credentials, and there is no in-app switch to prefer your own provider. Your own credentials are used only when hosted AI is unavailable, out of quota, or not enabled on your account. If you want every request to go directly to your own provider instead, ask us to disable premium hosted AI on your account.
privacyPage.sync.heading: Optional multi-device sync
privacyPage.sync.body: Multi-device sync lets your own computers share one set of records. It is off until you turn it on in the app, and it is available only with a Nixus Cloud account that includes multi-device sync. Until you enable it, nothing in this section applies to you.
privacyPage.sync.what: When sync is on, your changes travel continuously: once your edits settle, Nixus uploads them as a log of changes and, periodically, a full snapshot of that profile's database — budgets, transactions, accounts, income, assets, net worth history, vehicles, maintenance records, your in-app action history and your app settings. Full-size project images travel separately, so they never slow down a new computer's first load: the snapshot carries only their thumbnails and a fingerprint of each image, each full-size image is uploaded as its own object under that fingerprint, and a new computer downloads one the first time you ask to see it. Those image objects are protected exactly like the snapshot — TLS in transit, Amazon S3 server-side encryption (SSE-S3) at rest, and the same statement below applies to them: they are not end-to-end encrypted. Your other computers merge those changes field by field, with no question asked of you: when both computers changed the same field, the later change wins; when one deleted something another edited at the same time, the delete wins, and deleted items stay recoverable for 30 days; balances and counters are merged as additions, so two computers reacting to the same thing never double-count it. Edits you make offline are kept and sent when you are back online, and your action history travels as an append-only record that is never rewritten.
privacyPage.sync.notSynced: Some things are removed from the snapshot before it leaves your machine and are never uploaded: Nixus's own internal sync bookkeeping, and the settings that describe this computer's AI provider configuration. Your AI provider credentials are never part of it — they stay in your operating system's credential store and are never transmitted to Nixus. A profile you keep local-only is never uploaded at all.
privacyPage.sync.where: The copy is stored in a private storage bucket operated by Nixus on Amazon Web Services, in the US East (N. Virginia) region. Each account's data sits under its own separate location in that bucket, and an app can only ever reach the location belonging to the account signed in on it.
privacyPage.sync.protection: Transfers use TLS. At rest the copy is encrypted with Amazon S3 server-side encryption (SSE-S3), and each computer is given short-lived credentials scoped to that one account's location. Stated plainly, because it matters: this copy is not end-to-end encrypted. Nixus does not read your records, but a Nixus administrator with access to that AWS account could technically do so, and so could AWS. The stored format reserves a marker for an encryption scheme so a future version can add encryption that would rule this out; that encryption is not in place today.
privacyPage.sync.retention: Old change-log segments are deleted once a newer snapshot covers them, and the storage keeps previous versions of each object for 30 days before they expire, so a bad upload can be recovered from. A computer that has not synced for more than 90 days re-downloads the latest snapshot and re-applies the changes it had not sent yet. The current copy is kept for as long as sync is on, and it is kept — never deleted — if your account stops being eligible for sync.
privacyPage.sync.deletion: The app's only delete permission is the cleanup described above, inside your own location: it can remove change-log segments a newer snapshot already covers, and snapshots a newer one supersedes. It is deliberately given no permission to delete the record binding that location to your account, the pointers and roster your computers coordinate through, or your project images, so one of your computers cannot erase the copy the others depend on. In this first version there is still no way to delete the cloud copy from inside the app. To have the cloud copy deleted, email the address at the bottom of this page and ask; deletion is handled manually. Turning sync off in the app stops transfers but does not delete the copy.
privacyPage.sync.localOnly: If you never turn sync on, or you use a local-only profile, no sync code runs and nothing is uploaded: the promise above is unchanged for you.
termsPage.sync.heading: Multi-device sync
termsPage.sync.body: Multi-device sync is an optional feature of eligible Nixus Cloud accounts and is off until you turn it on. It is beta: its availability is not guaranteed, it may be changed, interrupted or withdrawn, and individual transfers may fail or be delayed. Nixus may suspend sync for an account, including for abuse or excessive cost. The Privacy Policy describes what is uploaded, where it is stored, and who can technically read it.
termsPage.sync.conflict: Sync merges your computers continuously rather than asking you to choose: changes are merged field by field, the later change to a field wins, a delete wins over an edit made at the same time, and balances and counters are merged as additions so nothing is double-counted. The one time Nixus does ask is the first time you link a computer that already has data of its own, and the cloud copy is never silently overwritten: you choose between loading the cloud copy — your current local file is kept as a dated backup — and keeping your local data and publishing it over the cloud copy. Restoring a backup or copying a profile relinks that computer and asks the same question. If a computer is running an older version of Nixus, it waits for the update before applying changes that version cannot read, and keeps working on your local data meanwhile. Deleting all data on one computer only unlinks that computer: the cloud copy and your other computers are untouched.
termsPage.sync.backups: Sync is not a backup service. The cloud copy exists so your own computers can share one set of records, and keeping your own backups remains your responsibility. In this version there is no way to delete the cloud copy from inside the app; turning sync off stops transfers but does not delete it. To request deletion, contact us at the address below.
termsPage.sync.freeze: If your account stops being eligible for sync, Nixus freezes it: uploads and downloads stop, the cloud copy is kept and not deleted, and the app keeps working normally with your local data. Becoming eligible again resumes sync.
